chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Safwan from Saif al-Tammarr said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'A man says to his wife,

key_terms.الظَّهْر: The back; refers to the specific Quranic formula for divorce declaration.
key_terms.الْأُمَّهَاتِ: The mothers; the specific relatives mentioned in the Quran for Zihar.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man says to his wife 'You are to me like the back of my aunt' instead of 'my mother'?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that while the Quran explicitly mentions 'mothers' in the context of *Zihar*, the juristic principle of *Qiyas* (analogy) extends the ruling to other female relatives like aunts, rendering the declaration forbidden (*Haram*) rather than a valid *Zihar*. This highlights the Shia scholarly approach of deriving specific legal nuances from the Quranic text while applying broader jurisprudential logic to ensure consistency in marital laws. The ruling underscores the importance of precise intention and linguistic scope in Islamic legal declarations.
